payload.abstract: In this parallel-group trial, 240 adults with mild hypertension were randomized to drug A or placebo. The primary outcome, change in systolic pressure at 12 weeks, favored drug A (difference -6.1 mmHg; p = 0.003).

We randomized 64 patients with chronic migraine to a two-period crossover of nerve stimulation and sham stimulation. Monthly headache days did not differ between periods (p = 0.41), so the primary endpoint was not met.

Thirty-two primary schools were randomized as clusters to a daily reading program or usual teaching; 1,850 pupils took part. Reading scores after one year, the primary outcome, were higher with the program (p < 0.001).
A total of 150 adults with acute low back pain were randomized to physiotherapy or advice alone. Pain at 6 weeks, the primary outcome, was similar in both groups (p = 0.62).
This pilot study randomized 40 older adults to tai chi or stretching classes. Balance scores improved in both groups. The abstract reports no formal test of the primary outcome.
In a parallel trial, 512 patients with heart failure were randomized to drug B or placebo. The primary composite outcome occurred less often with drug B (hazard ratio 0.78; p = 0.012).
We randomized 24 villages as clusters to water filters or no filters. Diarrhoea episodes in children under five, the primary outcome, fell by 31% with filters (p = 0.04).
Children with asthma (n = 96) were randomized in a crossover design to inhaler C and inhaler D for 4 weeks each. Peak flow, the primary outcome, was higher with inhaler C (p = 0.008).
A total of 300 adults with depression were randomized to an online therapy program or a waiting list. Symptom scores at 10 weeks, the primary outcome, were lower with online therapy (p = 0.001).

In this 2x2 factorial trial, 800 adults were randomized to vitamin D or placebo and to fish oil or placebo. Neither supplement reduced the rate of fractures, the primary outcome (p = 0.55 and p = 0.71).
We randomized adults with gout to drug E or drug F in parallel groups. Serum urate targets were reached more often with drug E. Enrolment and p values are given in the full report.

In a parallel trial, 180 patients after knee replacement were randomized to nerve block or standard pain relief. Opioid use in the first 48 hours, the primary outcome, was lower with the nerve block (p = 0.02).
Forty-eight hospital wards were randomized as clusters to a hand hygiene campaign or usual practice. Hospital-acquired infections, the primary outcome, did not differ (p = 0.33).
A total of 72 adults with eczema were randomized to cream G or a plain moisturizer in parallel groups. Itch scores at 4 weeks, the primary outcome, were lower with cream G (p = 0.03).
We randomized 420 pregnant women to a daily walking program or usual care. Gestational diabetes, the primary outcome, occurred in 9% and 11% of women (p = 0.37).
In a crossover trial, 30 adults with sleep apnea used mask H and mask I for two weeks each. Adherence, the primary outcome, was higher with mask H (p = 0.049).
A total of 1,200 adults over 65 were randomized to a high-dose or a standard-dose flu vaccine. Laboratory-confirmed influenza, the primary outcome, was less common with the high dose (p = 0.006).
This trial randomized 88 students to a smartphone sleep coach or a sleep leaflet. Sleep quality improved in both groups; the authors call the difference uncertain.

In a 2x2 factorial design, 640 adults with prediabetes were randomized to metformin or placebo and to a diet program or none. Progression to diabetes, the primary outcome, was lower with metformin (p = 0.01).
Sixty general practices were randomized as clusters to an antibiotic feedback letter or no letter. Antibiotic prescriptions over 6 months, the primary outcome, fell with the letter (p = 0.002).
